kyo_oshokuya_kappa.gf_detail: [WARNINGS (Greg, 2026-08-19): the shop serves GLUTEN-REDUCED beer — that is not celiac-safe and must be declined regardless of the all-GF menu. The gluten-free pizza crust is bought in from an outside supplier (Pizza Icaro), so crust safety is third-party, not this kitchen.] Japanese sources resolve the conflict in favor of a full conversion: since September 2024 the kitchen uses no wheat flour at all (小麦粉を一切つかわず), replacing wheat pasta and focaccia with house-made rice-flour (米粉) pasta and bread — the whole menu is now gluten-free. The owner's own blog does NOT admit wheat is still served; the sentence about wheat pasta/focaccia is a past-tense counterfactual ('we could have kept using them with no problem, but chose to convert'). Order anything, or ask for the グルテンフリーコース (50-vegetable GF course); note the restaurant still posts a contamination disclaimer (コンタミの可能性があるので小麦アレルギーに対応しておりません), so a strict celiac should self-identify and confirm seasonings/no cross-contact.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.vegan_detail: This is a vegetable-sommelier restaurant with strong produce focus, but it is emphatically NOT vegan — the menu is heavy on meat (Kameoka beef, lamb, chicken), fish/seafood and cheese, and the owner's blog worries customers wrongly assume it went vegan. Plant-forward options like the vegetable spaghetti/risotto and green salad can likely be made vegan on request (confirm no butter, cheese or dashi); arrange vegan needs in advance.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:30) / Dinner 17:30-22:00 (L.O. 21:30). Closed day reported inconsistently across sources (empacede: Tuesdays + irregular; some listings show Wednesday or Sunday) - treat as irregular and confirm.
kyo_oshokuya_kappa.notes: [GF] As of Sept 2024 the entire kitchen is wheat-flour-free — a genuine 100% conversion, not shared with a wheat line; pasta is rice-flour and bread is 米粉パン. Celiacs can eat broadly here, and the 50-vegetable グルテンフリーコース is the safest showcase order. The one caveat: the restaurant posts a contamination disclaimer and says it cannot formally guarantee against a wheat allergy, so self-identify as celiac and confirm cross-contact and sauces. Not vegetarian/vegan-oriented — plenty of meat, seafood and cheese.

roles: 野菜ソムリエ / Vegetable Sommelier
chef_bio.background: Ishibashi Kenji is the owner-chef of Oshokuya Kappa, described as the only Japan Vegetable Sommelier Association (日本野菜ソムリエ協会) certified restaurant in Kyoto. In a 14 September 2024 blog post he announced the restaurant's pivot to the concept 'グルテンフリーで叶える至福のイタリアン' (blissful Italian achieved through gluten-free), switching the kitchen to use no wheat flour. He is explicit that the change was voluntary — his business was thriving on wheat pasta and focaccia — motivated by learning about gluten's effects rather than being forced by an allergy.
chef_bio.philosophy: Delicious first, gluten-free second — as a craftsman he says '美味しく無いならグルテンフリーにする必要無い' (if it isn't delicious there's no point going gluten-free); he pledges the food is as tasty as before and centers seasonal Japanese vegetables via his sommelier training.
chef_bio.specialty: GF pasta (rice-flour), 米粉パン (rice-flour bread), and a 50-vegetable グルテンフリーコース

anecdotes.text: Cites tennis player Novak Djokovic overcoming gluten intolerance via a gluten-free diet and rising to world No.1 as inspiration for the switch.
Says he isn't wheat-allergic himself (only mild skin irritation) and is running a personal experiment of quitting wheat to see what changes.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The owner's own 2024-09-14 fcblog post announces a full conversion to gluten-free Italian using no wheat flour; the homepage repeats '小麦粉を一切つかわず' and the empacede GF guide rates it ★★★★★ with 'すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー' since Sept 2024. Note: empacede also states the shop does NOT accept wheat-allergy orders due to cross-contamination risk (コンタミの可能性) — so 'gluten-free' here means recipe-level, not celiac-safe.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Restaurant states 'コンタミの可能性があるので、小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' — cross-contamination is possible, so they do not formally accommodate a wheat allergy, despite the kitchen using no wheat flour.
Homepage repeats they serve gluten-free dishes with no wheat flour but explicitly '小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません' due to contamination risk (likely supplier/seasoning-level).

staff_allergy_handling.text: The restaurant openly declines to guarantee safety for a medical wheat allergy (小麦アレルギー未対応) even while marketing itself as fully gluten-free; strict celiacs should self-identify and confirm.

positives.text: Kitchen converted entirely to gluten-free in Sept 2024, using no wheat flour; wheat pasta and focaccia were replaced with house-made rice-flour pasta and 米粉パン.
Curated Japanese GF guide rates it ★★★★★ with 'all menu items gluten-free' (すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー).
Signature 50-vegetable gluten-free course by a certified vegetable sommelier.

owner_signoff.reason: Greg. Survives scrutiny: the owner states 「小麦粉を含め麦系は現在一切使用していません」, which rules out the spelt trap that caught another Kyoto record, and FindMeGlutenFree carries ~126 ratings including roughly two dozen symptomatic-celiac reviews all reporting no symptoms. Held at high rather than dedicated because the shop own site says it cannot accommodate wheat allergy.

gf_review.why: This was the flagged high-risk Italian record and I went at it hardest: I checked for surviving wheat pasta/focaccia, for a spelt-style 'still gluten' substitute, for shared pasta water, and for any glutening report in English or Japanese. All three fail to disprove. The owner's Sept-2024 blog post and the shop's Japanese AND English homepages confirm a full conversion (「小麦粉を一切つかわず」); the FindMeGlutenFree listing carries an owner statement going further — 「小麦粉を含め麦系は現在一切使用していません」 (no barley-family grains either, which rules out the spelt trap) — and the Hot Pepper menu page states 「当店のお料理はすべてグルテンフリーです」 with 自家製米粉パン. FMGF shows 126 recent ratings, 'reported to be dedicated gluten-free', community-reported 'dedicated gluten-free pasta pot and water', and I read roughly two dozen reviews from self-identified symptomatic celiacs — every single symptom field said 'No symptoms', with zero glutening reports found. It stays at `high` and NOT dedicated because the shop itself explicitly refuses to accommodate a medical wheat allergy.
red_flags: The shop's own site, in Japanese and English, explicitly declines wheat-allergy accommodation: 「小麦を使った料理はございませんが、わからないところで紛れ込んでしまう可能性もございますので、小麦アレルギーに対応はしておりません」 / 'we cannot accommodate wheat allergies'. This is why it must not be labelled dedicated

FMGF reported GF items include 'Beer (Gluten-Reduced)' — gluten-REDUCED (enzyme-treated barley) beer is NOT celiac-safe and is inconsistent with the owner's '麦系は一切使用していません' claim. A celiac must decline the beer
The GF pizza crust is bought in from an outside supplier (Pizza Icaro per a recent reviewer), so crust safety depends on a third party, not the kitchen
Owner frames the conversion as a health/lifestyle choice, not an allergy programme ('this is not because of allergies') — motivation is wellness, which historically correlates with looser protocol
Effectively a one-chef operation; multiple reviewers note the chef works alone, so protocol quality is entirely person-dependent
gf_review.plain_rice: Not a rice-bowl restaurant. Risotto is on the menu and is widely reported GF, and house-made 米粉 bread and rice croquettes are served, but plain unseasoned gohan is not a standard item — do not plan on it here.

kyo_senza_x.gf_detail: [Adversarial GF review 2026-08-19: high→ask. The gluten-free substance of this record survives — Tabelog's own listing text still reads 「当店は小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品を使用しないイタリア料理ベースのレストランです」 and kyotopi confirms imported corn/rice pasta, 米粉 bread, and that the inherited pizzeria wood oven is unused. What does NOT survive is that the place is operable. Tabelog carries the banner 「現在、スタッフ不足のため当面の間、休業しております」, and the official domain www.senza-x.com no longer serves the restaurant at all — it now returns an unrelated Korean sports-betting/toto page, and www.senza-x.com/en (its former booking page, still in search indexes) 404s. A lapsed domain plus a ~1-year staff-shortage 休業 (reservations stopped Sept 2025; this audit is Aug 2026) is functionally a closure, and an app must not route a celiac child to a shut door under a `high` badge.] Senza X describes itself as 「小麦・グルテン・卵・乳製品を使わないアレルギー対応のイタリア料理店」— a fully allergy-adapted Italian restaurant that uses no wheat, gluten, egg or dairy anywhere on the menu. Pasta is imported from Italy and made from corn and rice rather than wheat (「もちろんパスタはグルテンフリー」), and bread is baked from rice flour (「パンは米粉を使用したもの」), so the entire kitchen is free-from rather than offering modified dishes. IMPORTANT — current status: the venue is TEMPORARILY CLOSED (休業). Its Tabelog listing carries the banner 'Currently, we are temporarily closed due to staff shortages,' and its own booking system stopped accepting reservations from September 2025 onward; it has not been reported as permanently closed. Confirm reopening via the official site or Instagram before visiting.
kyo_senza_x.vegan_detail: The whole kitchen is egg- and dairy-free, and owner-chef Shiga's stated aim was a restaurant 'enjoyable by all, vegans and allergy sufferers,' so plant-based choices exist — e.g. 植物性乳酸菌のジェラート (plant-based probiotic gelato) and fruit sorbet (いちごのソルベ). However, most pasta and antipasti feature fish or meat (anchovy, sardine, clams, beef cheek, lamb), so it is options rather than a full vegan menu; ask when booking.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Shop advertises グルテンフリー as a product/ingredient claim but is a full patisserie also making wheat-flour items (roll cakes, baumkuchen, sandwich cookies); no no-wheat-on-premises or cross-contact statement found.
gf_cross_contamination.why: DEFECT, two ways. The three items named as the wheat ones (roll cake, baumkuchen, ganache sand cookies) are the RICE-FLOUR ones per their own 原材料 (米粉, no 小麦粉), and a cross-contact statement DOES exist: the baumkuchen carries 「本品製造工場では小麦を含む製品を生産しています」. Rewrite as: no wheat flour in the products, but

vegan_cross_contact.text: Many cakes contain dairy and eggs; vegan applies only to specific chocolates/raw items.

staff_allergy_handling.text: No published allergen-handling protocol; buyers must confirm per-item and about shared equipment directly.

positives.text: "白砂糖・添加物を使用しないチョコレート" and "グルテンフリーやオーガニックカカオといった素材にもこだわり"; sells 米粉ケーキ.

kyo_everysoy.gf_detail: This soy-milk specialty cafe run by long-established Kyoto yuba maker ゆば庄 makes its signature choux pastry from rice flour and soy cream. The menu page states the ソイシュークリーム base is 「米粉のシュー生地と豆乳クリーム」and is 「乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー」— but note the chocolate flavor is an exception: 「ショコラのチョコレートの中には一部乳成分が含まれます」(contains some dairy). It is a small takeout-focused counter (テイクアウト中心の小さなカフェ) that also sells non-gluten-free ライトミール from the same shared counter, so this is a dessert/drink stop with genuine GF options, not a fully GF venue; celiacs should treat cross-contact from shared prep/counter as possible.
kyo_everysoy.vegan_detail: Everything is built on soy milk and the shop centers on plant-based soy, but the rice-flour choux pastry is likely egg-based and some flavors contain dairy (chocolate). No explicit vegan labeling was found, so vegans should confirm egg/dairy per item.
kyo_everysoy.notes: [GF] Soy-milk cafe by Kyoto yuba maker ゆば庄. The signature 米粉シュークリーム (SOY chou à la crème) is stated 乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー — a reliable GF treat (avoid the chocolate flavor, which contains some dairy). Because non-GF light meals are prepared and sold from the same small counter, treat it as a GF-options dessert/drink stop rather than a celiac-safe kitchen.

roles: parent company: ゆば庄 (Yubasho / 京湯葉の老舗)
chef_bio.background: EVERYSOY is a soy-focused cafe brand created by ゆば庄 (Yubasho), a long-established Kyoto yuba (tofu-skin) specialist. The shop's own site states 「京都で長年湯葉をつくり続けてきた京湯葉の老舗『ゆば庄』が、厳選したフレッシュな豆乳を使ってつくっています」. The concept ('Stop, Soy'n Go') is to help people enjoy nutritious soy in everyday, approachable forms — drinks and sweets — rather than only traditional yuba. It runs a small takeout-centered counter cafe at its 四条烏丸 branch near the Shijo-Karasuma crossing.
chef_bio.philosophy: Make high-nutrition soy an everyday pleasure via fresh soy milk drinks and dairy-free sweets.
chef_bio.specialty: Soy-milk drinks and the rice-flour, dairy-free ソイシュークリーム (SOY chou à la crème) and ソイティラミス.

anecdotes.text: The SOY chou à la crème pairs a rice-flour choux shell with soy-milk cream, marketed as 『とっても軽くてクリーミー』.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: everysoy.com（公式ブランド・メニュー・店舗ページ）は、京湯葉の老舗『ゆば庄』が厳選フレッシュ豆乳で手がけるソイカフェで、米粉・乳不使用のソイシュークリームやソイティラミスを提供と記載。四条烏丸に店舗（食べログ EVERYSOY 四条烏丸店）。KBS京都ラジオも特集。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Small takeout counter that also sells non-GF ライトミール from the same counter; shared prep space means cross-contact is possible.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Dessert/drink focus; no wheat soy sauce implicated in the signature items.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Chocolate flavor contains some dairy: 「ショコラのチョコレートの中には一部乳成分が含まれます」.

positives.text: Signature ソイシュークリーム explicitly labeled 乳製品不使用・グルテンフリー with a 米粉 (rice-flour) choux base.

kyo_loco_chicken.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. A Hawaiian-style mochiko/rice-flour chicken specialist. The Japanese GF guide jp.japan-glutenfree.com (rated ★★★★) states 「米粉チキン専門店です。米粉チキンは、小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使っており、グルテンフリーです」— the karaage is battered in rice flour, not wheat. Burgers can be made GF: 「ハンバーガーのバンズは、プラス200円で、グルテンフリーのバンズに変更できます」and tacos/taco rice are inherently GF. The guide notes wheat is present on-site only for standard burger buns and for beer; a shared fryer is likely at a general fried-chicken shop, so confirm dedicated oil and no wheat in the seasoning before ordering, and note the on-premises beer keeps this out of dedicated-GF territory.
kyo_loco_chicken.vegan_detail: A fried-chicken and burger shop; core menu is chicken. No vegan mains identified.
kyo_loco_chicken.notes: [GF] Rice-flour (mochiko) chicken specialist near Shijo-Kawaramachi. Per JP GF guide, the karaage/chicken uses rice flour instead of wheat (グルテンフリー), burgers swap to a GF bun for +¥200, and tacos/taco rice are GF. Wheat on-site is limited to standard buns and beer — but it is a small (5-seat) general fried-chicken shop, so confirm the fryer oil isn't shared with any wheat item and that seasonings are wheat-free before you order.

chef_bio.background: LOCO CHICKEN is a Hawaiian-influenced 米粉チキン (rice-flour / mochiko chicken) specialist that opened around 30 September 2021, about a 3-minute walk south of Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station in the Shijo-Kawaramachi area (河原町会館). It is a tiny first-come, first-served counter shop (5 seats) doing dine-in and takeout, blending Hawaiian 'mochiko chicken' style with Kyoto tastes; the Kyoto-native owner drew inspiration from Saipan's 'LOCO & TACO.' The signature is thin, light, crisp rice-flour-battered chicken served as burgers or over-rice plates.
chef_bio.philosophy: Light, crisp mochiko/rice-flour chicken in a casual Hawaiian plate-lunch format.
chef_bio.specialty: 米粉唐揚げ (rice-flour karaage) plates and chicken burgers with an optional gluten-free bun (+¥200).

anecdotes.text: Menu spans classic, yangnyeom, Nashville-hot and yuzu-pepper tartar chicken burgers plus 3- and 4-piece rice plates.
米粉チキンは小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使いグルテンフリー。ハンバーガーのバンズはプラス200円でグルテンフリーのバンズに変更でき、席数はカウンター5席のみ。

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: jp.japan-glutenfree.com（京都GFリスト、★★★★、米粉チキン専門店・GFバンズ+200円・カウンター5席）、osumituki.com（2021/9/30オープン・住所・価格・サイパンLOCO & TACO由来）、食べログ/Retty 掲載が一致。

gf_cross_contamination.text: Small general fried-chicken shop; a shared fryer is likely. Guide states wheat on-site is limited to burger buns and beer, but fryer/seasoning cross-contact is unconfirmed — ask before ordering.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Sauces/glazes (yangnyeom, teriyaki-style) may contain wheat soy sauce; confirm per item.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: The page names a yangnyeom sauce but says nothing about soy sauce, wheat or allergens, and never mentions teriyaki - the wheat-soy-sauce caution is the record's inference. Either mark it as inference or cite the shop directly. Side note: this article calls the coating 餅粉 (glutinous rice flour), not

staff_allergy_handling.text: Offers a paid GF bun swap (+¥200), indicating some allergy awareness, but no formal cross-contact protocol documented.

positives.text: 米粉チキン専門店です。米粉チキンは、小麦粉の代わりに米粉を使っており、グルテンフリーです — rated ★★★★ by JP GF guide.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

kyo_nicole_naturelle.gf_detail: THE NICOLE is a conventional Kyoto patisserie that also runs a separate allergen-free sub-line, Nicole Naturelle, whose sweets are made with 100% domestic rice flour and no wheat. The venue's own site states 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』 and describes the line as 『卵、乳、白砂糖不使用』『グルテンフリー』『ヴィーガンスイーツ』 using 国産米粉100%. However, the SAME shop bakes ordinary wheat flour cakes and serves 欧風スパイスカレー (European-style spice curry, typically a wheat-roux base), so the kitchen is shared and cross-contact with wheat flour is a real risk — celiacs must confirm the item is from the Naturelle line and ideally order it pre-made/sealed. Because of the shared wheat kitchen this stays an 'options' venue, not a dedicated GF facility.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.vegan_detail: The Nicole Naturelle line is fully plant-based — 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用, using 京豆腐 (Kyoto tofu), 豆乳ヨーグルト (soy yogurt), soy-based 'butter', coconut oil and maple syrup in place of dairy and eggs. These items are explicitly marketed as ヴィーガンスイーツ. The parent THE NICOLE shop, though, also sells conventional cakes with egg/dairy and non-vegan curry, so only the Naturelle line is vegan — choose from it specifically.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.hours_raw: 10:30-16:00; closed Mondays and Tuesdays (per the venue's own site). Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are by reservation / online order only. Hours differ between sources (Tabelog lists Mon-Fri 10:30-18:00, Sat 10:30-17:00, closed Sun) - confirm before visiting.
kyo_nicole_naturelle.notes: [GF] The Nicole Naturelle sub-line uses 国産米粉100% and no wheat, but it is baked in the same kitchen as THE NICOLE's ordinary wheat cakes and wheat-roux spice curry — treat as cross-contact risk, not celiac-safe. Order Naturelle items specifically (they are reservation/online-order only, sold mostly as whole tarts, chocolate and sablé tins) and confirm the item is from the allergen line. Cash only; small counter shop in the Horikawa shopping arcade.

chef_bio.background: Owner-pâtissier 堀口微笑琉 was born in 1979 in Kyoto's Nishijin district and trained at several patisseries between 1999 and 2006 before opening his own shop, 洋菓子屋Sorcier, in Umeda in 2008. The business relocated and evolved over the years — becoming Kitchen&Cake NICOLE in 2015 and rebranding as THE NICOLE at the current 西陣 (Nishijin) location in 2019. In 2022 he added a spice-curry operation (麺屋 微笑琉 / NICOLEカレー, a once-a-week spice-curry-udon venture), and in 2023 he launched the Nicole Naturelle allergen-free, vegan, gluten-free sweets line. The shop's stated aim is 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」— sweets that people with dietary restrictions can also enjoy.
chef_bio.philosophy: A hybrid patisserie-and-curry café built around inclusivity and low-sugar / low-fat, 'body-friendly' sweets, with the Nicole Naturelle line created so that people with egg, dairy and wheat restrictions can still enjoy cakes.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) vegan gluten-free tarts, 京豆腐 tofu-based raw-chocolate confections and 黒糖 sablé tins; also European-style spice curry.

anecdotes.text: The venture is a 洋菓子×スパイスカレー hybrid — a Western-confectionery shop that also serves a meat-free 'Nicole curry' deriving umami from vegetables, plus rotating daily creative spice curries.
The allergen-free Nicole Naturelle line was launched in 2023, years after the base patisserie, specifically to serve customers with dietary restrictions.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: the-nicole.com（自社サイト沿革）に、オーナー堀口微笑琉（1979年西陣生まれ、1999-2006修業、2008 Sorcier梅田、2015 Kitchen&Cake NICOLE、2019 THE NICOLE西陣、2022 麺屋微笑琉、2023 Nicole Naturelle）、Nicole Naturelleの「卵・乳製品・小麦粉・動物性油脂不使用」「グルテンフリー」「ヴィーガン」「国産米粉100%」の記載あり。kyotopi.jpは洋菓子×スパイスカレーのハイブリッド業態を紹介。食べログは住所・営業時間・現金のみを裏付け。

gf_cross_contamination.text: The Nicole Naturelle allergen-free sweets are baked in the same premises as THE NICOLE's conventional wheat-flour cakes and a wheat-roux European-style spice curry, so shared-kitchen cross-contact with wheat is a genuine risk despite the rice-flour recipes.
Venue's own claim for the line: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』／『グルテンフリー』／国産米粉100%. No dedicated-facility or cross-contamination protocol is stated.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable to the sweets line; however the shop's spice curry is not part of the gluten-free line and should be assumed to contain wheat (欧風カレー roux) — do not treat curry as GF.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Nicole Naturelle items are made in a kitchen that also handles dairy, eggs and animal fats for conventional cakes; the Naturelle line itself is 卵・乳・動物性油脂不使用 but shared equipment means trace animal-product contact is possible.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop positions itself as making 「食材の制限がある方も楽しめるスイーツ」and takes Naturelle items ご予約のみ (by reservation), suggesting allergy awareness, but no formal celiac cross-contact handling procedure is documented.

positives.text: Explicit written wheat-free claim using 100% domestic rice flour: 『卵、乳製品、小麦粉、動物性油脂は使用しておりません』『グルテンフリー』, a dedicated recipe line rather than incidental GF items.
Naturelle line is fully vegan (京豆腐, 豆乳ヨーグルト, ココナッツオイル), doubling as a good option for plant-based celiacs.

kyo_oubon.gf_detail: OUBON is a conventional Western pâtisserie near Fushimi Inari that sells regular wheat cakes AND a separate allergy-oriented 米粉 (rice-flour) line, so wheat is handled in the same kitchen. The shop's own claim for the rice-flour line reads: 「全てに米粉を使用していますのでアレルギーをお持ちの方でも、もちろん食べていただけます」 ("Everything uses rice flour, so even those with allergies can of course eat it"). Because the same bakery also produces wheat pastries daily, cross-contact with gluten is a real risk and this cannot be treated as celiac-safe — confirm with staff and buy only the labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー items.
kyo_oubon.vegan_detail: The rice-flour items are not vegan: the shop lists 卵 (egg) and 乳 (dairy) as allergens on its gluten-free products. The signature 豆乳米粉ロール is described as 「グルテンフリー商品となっており、アレルギー物質は卵、乳」 and uses Hokkaido cream (whipped with soymilk), so egg and dairy remain. No vegan line is advertised.
kyo_oubon.hours_raw: 10:00–20:00, closed Wednesdays (some listings show Wed 12:00–18:00). Tel 075-632-8287.
kyo_oubon.notes: [GF] Not celiac-safe — this is a shared wheat kitchen. OUBON bakes conventional wheat cakes alongside its 米粉 (rice-flour) allergy line, so gluten cross-contact is likely; only the explicitly labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー sweets (e.g. 豆乳米粉ロール, 米粉フィナンシェ, 米粉マドレーヌ) are wheat-free by recipe, and even those are baked in the same premises. Also note the GF items contain egg and dairy. Tabelog currently lists the shop's operating status as unconfirmed/on-hold, so phone ahead (075-632-8287) to confirm it is open before visiting.

roles: Head pastry chef (シェフパティシエ)
chef_bio.background: OUBON opened in December 2017 a few minutes' walk from Fushimi Inari station in Fukakusa, Fushimi-ku. Head pastry chef and owner Nobuo Kakine (垣根信夫) is described as a veteran patissier with 40 years of experience in Kyoto, having served as head pâtissier at a well-known hotel and other shops before opening his own. The shop is credited as being run by a pâtissier who helped pioneer Japanese-style (和風) sweets. For its gluten-free line OUBON sources rice flour from Asahi Seifunjo (朝日製粉所) in the Kyoto Tamba/Nantan area.
chef_bio.philosophy: To make rice-flour cakes so close to wheat versions that they are hard to tell apart in a blind test, so that people with wheat allergies can enjoy ordinary-tasting Western sweets alongside everyone else.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour (米粉) gluten-free cakes and baked sweets — signature 豆乳米粉ロール, plus financiers and madeleines — alongside a conventional wheat pâtisserie range.

anecdotes.text: The shop says its rice-flour sponge is so like wheat that even a blind taste test can't reveal the difference: 「小麦を使っているケーキと食感は全く同じで、味もブラインドテストをしてもわからないほど」.
OUBON's gluten-free cakes are made with rice flour supplied by Asahi Seifunjo, a Kyoto Tamba (Nantan) flour mill that profiled the shop and its 40-year-veteran chef.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: オーボンは2017年12月に伏見稲荷近くにオープンした洋菓子店。シェフパティシエの垣根信夫氏は京都で40年の実績を持つベテランで、有名ホテルのチーフパティシエを歴任。通常の小麦のケーキに加え、朝日製粉所の米粉を使ったアレルギー対応・グルテンフリーのケーキを製造。元祖和風スイーツを編み出したパティシエとして紹介されている。

gf_cross_contamination.text: OUBON is a conventional pâtisserie that handles both wheat cakes and rice-flour cakes: 「通常の小麦を使ったケーキや洋菓子、グルテンフリーなケーキやスイーツなどを扱っているお店」. Shared wheat kitchen means airborne-flour and shared-equipment cross-contact risk; not celiac-safe.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Not applicable — this is a dessert/patisserie shop; no savory soy-sauce dishes on offer.

vegan_cross_contact.text: GF items are not vegan by recipe — egg (卵) and dairy (乳) are listed as allergens on the rice-flour products, so vegan cross-contact is moot.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop markets the rice-flour line as 「アレルギー対応の米粉ケーキ」 (allergy-conscious rice-flour cakes) and states allergens for the roll as egg and dairy, indicating some allergen awareness, but no dedicated-line or celiac protocol is claimed.

positives.text: A named, clearly-labeled 米粉/グルテンフリー range (roll, financiers, madeleines, shortcake, lemon cake) with rice flour sourced from Asahi Seifunjo, made by a 40-year-veteran chef — a convenient wheat-free sweet stop right by Fushimi Inari.

tosaya_muroto.gf_detail: A Tosa (Kōchi) izakaya built on charcoal yakitori and seared bonito (katsuo tataki) — soy sauce, yakitori tare and ponzu (all typically wheat-based) run through the menu, so it is not celiac-safe by default. Some items can be gluten-free if confirmed: sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu. But the shared charcoal grill, shared fryer and wheat-containing sauces make cross-contamination likely — order shio, skip the tare/ponzu, and show the celiac card.
tosaya_muroto.vegan_detail: A Tosa seafood-and-yakitori counter: seared bonito, charcoal chicken, and shamo (game-fowl) hot pot. Bonito dashi and fish run through almost everything, so even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. A few plain vegetable skewers or pickles may be possible, but confirm dashi/bonito with the chef. Not a vegan destination.
tosaya_muroto.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00. Closed Sunday. (Some listings also note the 2nd & 3rd Monday closed and lunch by reservation only — confirm before visiting.)
tosaya_muroto.notes: [Mom & Pop — a Tosa master, ~50 years at the counter] A tiny Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo — up on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter plus one small tatami (6–8). The chef, a Tosa native with roughly half a century behind the grill, cooks yakitori over Tosa binchōtan charcoal and serves Kōchi's signature seared bonito (katsuo tataki), shamo (game-fowl) hot pot, and seasonal Tosa dishes. Reviewers praise thick, odorless bonito and carefully grilled skewers, and a charming old-Kyoto exterior; it draws locals and food-loving visitors alike. Reservations accepted (HotPepper). Address: 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49 (entrance on Kiyamachi-dōri). Instagram @tosayamuroto.

chef_bio.origin: Tosa (Kōchi Prefecture); the shop is in Kiyamachi, Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto
chef_bio.background: A Tosa (Kōchi) native who by most accounts has spent roughly fifty years cooking, running a small counter izakaya devoted to the food of his home region. He grills over Tosa binchōtan (the prized white charcoal of Kōchi) and centers the menu on Kōchi's most famous dish, seared bonito — the kind of veteran, single-counter kitchen where the chef works in front of you and the seasons drive what's served.
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal yakitori over Tosa binchōtan and Kōchi's signature katsuo (bonito) tataki, plus shamo (game-fowl) hot pot and seasonal Tosa dishes.

anecdotes.text: Regulars single out the bonito tataki as thick, generous and completely free of any fishy odor — the hallmark of well-handled katsuo — and note that each yakitori skewer is grilled with real care over binchōtan.

The shop is described as an izakaya serving 'the finest yakitori in Kyoto' by a chef with about 50 years of experience, originally from Tosa in Kōchi Prefecture, with a charming, old-Kyoto exterior that draws both locals and foreign guests.
It sits on Kiyamachi just south of Sanjo, upstairs on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant — an easy-to-miss counter that rewards those who seek it out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Japanese listings (Tabelog 郷土料理/焼き鳥, Retty, hitosara, navikyo, HotPepper) describe 土佐屋室戸 as a small Kōchi (Tosa) izakaya at 河原町通三条下ル大黒町49, entrance on Kiyamachi, on the 2nd floor above an Italian restaurant, with a ~10-seat counter and one small tatami room (6–8). Open Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00, closed Sunday; phone 075-221-3056; reservations accepted. The taishō, a Tosa native, is credited with ~50 years of experience; signatures are binchōtan yakitori, katsuo (bonito) tataki, and shamo hot pot, with seasonal Kōchi fare.

cultural_comfort.note: A small veteran-run counter on Kiyamachi that does see foreign diners and takes online reservations — but it's a Japanese izakaya led by a ~50-year chef, with little to no English. A reservation, a few words of Japanese, and easy counter manners go a long way.

gf_cross_contamination.text: This is a yakitori-and-izakaya counter, not a celiac-safe kitchen. Skewers are grilled over a shared charcoal grill alongside tare-basted (wheat soy sauce) items, and any battered/fried dishes share oil, so cross-contamination with wheat is likely across the menu.

Naturally gluten-free choices may exist if confirmed — sashimi, salt (shio) skewers, and salt-style katsuo tataki without ponzu — but they must be ordered explicitly shio/no-sauce and confirmed with the chef.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Yakitori tare, ponzu for the katsuo tataki, and nabe broths are built on Japanese soy sauce, which typically contains wheat. Assume these sauces contain gluten unless the chef confirms a wheat-free alternative; ordering shio (salt) avoids the tare.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A fish- and meat-forward Tosa izakaya (bonito, chicken, game-fowl hot pot) with bonito dashi throughout — even vegetable dishes likely carry animal-derived stock. There is no documented vegan menu; confirm each item with the chef.

positives.text: A tiny, owner-run counter where the chef cooks directly in front of you, so you can ask about ingredients and preparation face-to-face — easiest with some Japanese or a translation app.
